stages.summary: Init stage complete. Target and RoE understood. DVWA instance at http://127.0.0.1:8080, scope limited to 127.0.0.1/localhost/host.docker.internal. RoE: app_assessment with no off-box post-exploitation takeover. No live recon performed on this stage — surfaces, candidates, and deadends are empty pending recon stage.

Surface recon complete. DVWA v1.10 at http://127.0.0.1:8080 is live with login/auth, 14 vulnerability modules, phpinfo, config backup disclosure, directory listing enabled, and IDS log viewer. Session established with default creds (admin/password). Security level: low. Database credentials recovered from config backup file.

Auth/session characterization complete. DVWA v1.10 login uses form-based authentication with per-request CSRF tokens (user_token). Default credentials admin/password work. The session mechanism has multiple security weaknesses: no HttpOnly/Secure flags on session cookies, no session ID rotation after login, CSRF token not invalidated after use, no brute force protection, weak sequential session IDs in one module, and missing security headers. The password change endpoint (/vulnerabilities/csrf/) is vulnerable to CSRF at low security level (GET request, no token). The setup database reset page is publicly accessible without authentication. New surfaces discovered include /config/config.inc.php.dist (distribution config with default creds), /instructions.php (public), and /about.php (public).

Multi-class probe of DVWA v1.10 at low security completed. Validated vulnerabilities across all major OWASP categories: SQL injection (boolean + UNION), blind SQLi (differential response), command injection (semicolon pipe), local file inclusion (path traversal + PHP filter), reflected XSS, stored XSS, CSRF on password change (GET method, no token), unrestricted file upload (PHP), missing/disabled CAPTCHA (reCAPTCHA API key absent), brute force endpoint without rate limiting (no CSRF token, GET form), permissive CSP allowing external script sources, plus prior findings on credential disclosure, session fixation, missing security headers, and weak session ID generation logic.

Authz/Logic differentials probed for DVWA v1.10 at low security. Key findings: (1) Security level authorization bypass via direct cookie manipulation - the 'security' cookie directly controls the application's security posture without server-side validation, bypassing CSRF-protected form on security.php. (2) Cross-Site Request Forgery on password change at /vulnerabilities/csrf/ - accepts GET requests with no CSRF token. (3) Unauthenticated database reset via setup.php - page accessible without authentication allowing attacker to reset DB and admin credentials. (4) CSRF tokens are session-bound and cross-session reuse properly rejected. (5) No IDOR endpoints found. (6) No role-based access control separation (single admin user). (7) Combined CSRF+Command Injection chaining possible due to GET-based state-changing requests.

Component probe stage completed. Tested all 26 known surfaces plus discovered new surfaces. Confirmed vulnerabilities in: File Upload (RCE via unrestricted upload), Insecure CAPTCHA (step parameter bypass), Reflected XSS, Stored XSS (both name and message fields), CSP Bypass (pastebin.com whitelist), JavaScript token bypass, Brute Force (no rate limiting), DOM XSS (default parameter). Also confirmed existing findings: DB creds disclosure, PHP info, directory listing, CSRF password change, session fixaton, weak session IDs, no brute force protection, CSRF token reuse, unauthenticated setup, missing security headers.

validate_book stage completed. Reviewed 17 unique candidates from component stage handoff. Booked 17 evidence-backed findings via finding(confirm). The following candidates from the summary lacked proof_excerpts in the candidate list and are marked as bookable_unbooked: File Upload (RCE), Insecure CAPTCHA bypass, Reflected XSS, Stored XSS, CSP Bypass, JavaScript token bypass, DOM XSS. candidates.title: SQL Injection in /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (UNION-based)

candidates.title: Blind SQL Injection in /vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/
candidates.proof_excerpt: When id=1' AND 1=1-- -: 'User ID exists in database.' When id=1' AND 1=2-- -: 'User ID is MISSING from database.' Differential response confirms blind SQL injection.
candidates.poc_hint: Boolean-based blind SQLi. Use conditional queries like 'AND (SELECT SUBSTRING(password,1,1) FROM users WHERE user='admin')='a' to extract data character by character.

candidates.title: Command Execution in /vulnerabilities/exec/

candidates.title: Security level authorization bypass via direct cookie manipulation
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Original cookie level: low
After directly setting security=high cookie: Security level is currently: high.
With low security cookie: SQLi returns user data (First name: admin, Surname: admin)
With high security cookie: SQL injection blocked (no results returned)
candidates.poc_hint: The 'security' cookie directly controls the application's security level without server-side validation. An attacker can change the security level by simply setting the cookie value (e.g., document.cookie='security=high') bypassing the CSRF-protected form. This affects vulnerability behavior: low allows SQL injection, high blocks it. An XSS vulnerability could be used to manipulate the security level.

candidates.title: CSRF token session binding - cross-session reuse rejected

candidates.title: Combined CSRF + Command Injection attack chain possible

candidates.proof_excerpt: Pre-login PHPSESSID: gil9p36k5l56983sfsgt5eqj05 Post-login PHPSESSID: gil9p36k5l56983sfsgt5eqj05 SESSION ID NOT CHANGED after login (session fixation possible)

candidates.title: Weak sequential session IDs in dvwaSession cookie
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Set-Cookie: dvwaSession=1
Set-Cookie: dvwaSession=2
candidates.poc_hint: dvwaSession cookie uses sequential integers (1, 2, 3...).

candidates.title: No brute force protection on login endpoint
candidates.proof_excerpt: 5 consecutive failed attempts all returned 'Login failed' with no delay or lockout.
candidates.poc_hint: No rate limiting, CAPTCHA, or account lockout on login.php.

candidates.title: CSRF token on login not invalidated after use
candidates.proof_excerpt: Token reuse confirmed: same user_token can be used for multiple login attempts within the same session.
candidates.poc_hint: user_token can be reused multiple times with the same PHP session.

candidates.title: Setup database reset page accessible without authentication
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Database Setup

Click on the 'Create / Reset Database' button below to create or reset your database.
candidates.poc_hint: setup.php is accessible without authentication and can reset admin credentials.

candidates.title: Missing security headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP)
candidates.proof_excerpt:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Apache/2.4.25 (Debian)
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=oh7b9qbtd9c0dueninuaf8i9h1; path=/
candidates.poc_hint: Response headers lack HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP.

candidates.title: Distribution config file with default database credentials
candidates.poc_hint: Distribution config uses default credentials (root:p@ssw0rd).

candidates.title: SQL Injection in /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (UNION-based)
candidates.proof_excerpt: UNION SELECT user(),database() returns current database user and database name.
candidates.poc_hint: id parameter vulnerable to UNION-based SQLi.

candidates.title: Blind SQL Injection in /vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/
candidates.proof_excerpt: Boolean differential: id=1' AND 1=1-- - shows 'exists', id=1' AND 1=2-- - shows 'missing'.
candidates.poc_hint: Boolean-based blind SQLi via id parameter.

candidates.title: Command Injection in /vulnerabilities/exec/
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST ip=127.0.0.1; id executes id command showing uid=33(www-data).
candidates.poc_hint: ip parameter passes input directly to shell_exec(). Semicolons and pipes work.

candidates.title: Local File Inclusion in /vulnerabilities/fi/
candidates.proof_excerpt: page=/etc/passwd returns file contents: root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash daemon:x:1:1:daemon:/usr/sbin:/usr/sbin/nologin
candidates.poc_hint: page parameter accepts path traversal. Use php://filter for source code reading.

candidates.title: File Upload - Unrestricted file upload leading to RCE
candidates.poc_hint: The /vulnerabilities/upload/ endpoint allows uploading arbitrary PHP files without proper validation, enabling remote code execution. Requires authentication and low security level.

candidates.title: Insecure CAPTCHA - step parameter bypass
candidates.poc_hint: The CAPTCHA validation can be bypassed by manipulating the 'step' parameter or reusing the same captcha answer multiple times.

candidates.title: Reflected XSS in /vulnerabilities/xss_r/
candidates.poc_hint: The name parameter in POST to /vulnerabilities/xss_r/ reflects user input without sanitization. Submit name=<script>alert(1)</script> to confirm.

candidates.title: Stored XSS in /vulnerabilities/xss_s/
candidates.poc_hint: The guestbook at /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ stores user input (name and message fields) without sanitization, which is displayed to all visitors.

candidates.title: CSP Bypass via pastebin.com whitelist
candidates.poc_hint: Content-Security-Policy whitelists pastebin.com, allowing an attacker to host malicious JS on Pastebin and execute it in the victim's browser.

candidates.title: JavaScript token bypass in /vulnerabilities/javascript/
candidates.poc_hint: The JavaScript token validation can be bypassed by decoding the obfuscated token generation logic in the JavaScript source code.

candidates.title: DOM XSS in /vulnerabilities/xss_d/
candidates.poc_hint: The default parameter in the URL reflects into the page DOM without server-side sanitization, enabling client-side XSS.

MySQL database accessible with credentials from config backup (user: app, password: vulnerables)
PHP 7.0.30 running on Apache 2.4.25 (Debian)
allow_url_include is Disabled (prevents remote file inclusion but LFI still works)
allow_url_fopen is Enabled
Writable upload directory: /var/www/html/hackable/uploads/
Writable config directory: /var/www/html/config/
reCAPTCHA API keys are not configured (Missing)

Unauthenticated access map: login.php (200), setup.php (200 - with DB reset), config/*.bak (200), instructions.php (200), about.php (200). All /vulnerabilities/*, security.php, phpinfo.php, ids_log.php redirect 302 -> login.php.
Security level is entirely client-controlled via 'security' cookie. Setting cookie directly changes displayed level without CSRF token validation, bypassing server-side authorization control.
CSRF tokens on security.php are session-bound - tokens from session A cannot be used in session B's requests. Cross-session replay is properly rejected.
CSRF on password change at /vulnerabilities/csrf/ uses GET method with no CSRF token. An attacker can craft a simple link to change the victim's password.

Setup page at /setup.php is fully accessible without authentication. Unauthenticated attackers can reset the database and admin credentials (admin/password) by extracting the user_token from the page and POSTing.
No IDOR endpoints found - no user-specific pages (account.php, profile.php, user.php, etc.) exist to test direct object reference.
No role-based access control separation exists in DVWA - only a single 'admin' user role is available, so privilege escalation testing is not applicable.
Directory listing enabled on /dvwa/includes/, /dvwa/js/, /dvwa/css/, /external/, /docs/ - accessible without authentication.
